sablelightoverhaul.lightsource.title: Static Light Source
sablelightoverhaul.lightsource.pageHint: Mode 0 unregisters; radius 0 is derived from brightness; cloud reach 0 follows the client setting. Flood lighting resembles vanilla block light; ray lighting uses the shaped light field. Emitting faces apply only to spherical lights; the source cell is unaffected. Vanilla uses the vanilla block-light color (the default, matching a nearby torch); Warm uses the warmer client overlay color. Enter 6 hexadecimal digits below the palette to override it, or clear the box to use the palette again. Registered lights that have not been replaced by an SLO light block do not cast shadows (the shadow value reads 0); their brightness is set on this page. An AFN frequency board replaces redstone with the channel signal; all three control modes, including rising-edge toggle, still apply. Shift-right-click with the registration tool to take over or restore a light. Shift-right-click with an empty hand to configure any registered light.
sablelightoverhaul.lightsource.conesHint: Format: {hStart,hEnd,vStart,vEnd}; group with semicolons, up to 4 groups; h 0~360, v -90~90 (degrees, 1.4 per step). Empty = casts in every direction. Ranges that cross 0 must be written as two groups (315~360 and 0~45). Outside the cone a lamp does not cast, so light passes through; only inside does it occlude, and a narrow cone is cheaper.
sablelightoverhaul.lightsource.blinkHint: Format: on,off,on,off... (ticks, 1~1200 each, up to 16 segments). Example: 4,4 = on 4, off 4; 4,4,4,28 = a two second cycle. Empty = steady. A half-typed pattern is not saved and the box turns red.

sablelightoverhaul.spotlight.lore.0: Empty hand right-click = its settings page (control mode, colour, brightness, cone width, aim, range, falloff); with the registrar tool, right-click cycles the falloff profile and sneak-right-click hides or shows the model
sablelightoverhaul.spotlight.lore.1: Control mode 0 full redstone (bottom = brightness, top = width, sides = colour) / 1 redstone switch / 2 manual / 3 AFN channel
sablelightoverhaul.spotlight.lore.2: With an AFN board in hand: right-click to bind the channel, sneak-right-click to clear it. The settings live on the block, so everyone sees the same lamp
sablelightoverhaul.registrar.lore.0: Right-click a block that is emitting light = register it and cycle the mode (unregister / enabled / forced on); a block that emits nothing is refused. On a spotlight the same click cycles its falloff profile instead
sablelightoverhaul.registrar.lore.1: Sneak-right-click = take over: the block's own vanilla light goes off and this mod colours it instead; sneak-right-click again restores it. A block carrying a block entity is refused, because taking it over would lose what it holds
sablelightoverhaul.registrar.lore.2: A registered lamp: right-click with an empty hand opens its page (brightness, colour, radius, shadows, redstone control, AFN channel)
sablelightoverhaul.dustgenerator.lore.0: Physics bodies only. Right-click opens its page: speed to dust amount, lifetime, size, stretch, upward speed, search depth
sablelightoverhaul.dustgenerator.lore.1: The page's continuous-emission switch is for tuning while parked: it emits without the vehicle moving
sablelightoverhaul.smokegenerator.lore.0: Physics bodies only. Right-click opens its page: redstone signal to cadence and count, vent aim (yaw/pitch), speed, lifetime, size
sablelightoverhaul.smokegenerator.lore.1: The smoke lives in world space: the vehicle leaves it behind
Physics bodies only. Register blocks with the vortex marker (they belong to the nearest vortex generator on that body); any movement, climbing included, mists the registered surface towards the generator
Right-click opens its page: rate, flow towards the generator, spread, lift. No threshold: any movement mists
sablelightoverhaul.vortexwand.lore.0: Right-click a block to register it, left-click to take it back out
sablelightoverhaul.vortexwand.lore.1: Sneak-right-click sets a corner, a second sneak-right-click fills the box (air is skipped); sneak-left-click sets a corner the same way and its second click fills the box to remove
sablelightoverhaul.vortexwand.lore.2: While held, the registered blocks are outlined: cyan = registered, gold = the generator, orange = the pending corner
sablelightoverhaul.dustmarker.lore.0: Marks which body's surfaces the dust coming off the vehicle should land on
sablelightoverhaul.dustmarker.lore.1: No collision; a wrench hides or shows its model without losing the marking
sablelightoverhaul.lightsource.lore.0: Sneak-right-click a block to turn it into an invisible light source: the block keeps its own look and only its vanilla light is switched off (the item is not consumed). A block carrying a block entity is refused
sablelightoverhaul.lightsource.lore.1: Sneak-right-click a disguised block to restore it; a stand-in placed by hand has no original, so there that gesture opens its page instead, as does a plain right-click with an empty hand
sablelightoverhaul.lightsource.lore.2: Redstone control: ignore / level / rising edge / AFN channel (a channel holds its value, so no edge is used)
sablelightoverhaul.disco.lore.0: Right-click opens its page: beam count, colour list, spin, range, per-beam width, intensity, falloff
sablelightoverhaul.disco.lore.1: Modes: 0 ignore redstone / 1 latch / 2 powered / 3 AFN channel. The settings live on the ball, so everyone watches the same show
sablelightoverhaul.flashlight.lore.0: Right-click toggles it; sneak-right-click opens its page (operators only)
sablelightoverhaul.flashlight.lore.1: Its page: colour, range step, width in degrees, decay speed, decay curve, beam brightness, point radius, point brightness
sablelightoverhaul.flashlight.lore.2: Casts shadows on its own beam by default (needs the Advanced tier and a patched shader pack); other players' flashlights are drawn within flashlight.syncRange (48 blocks by default) but do not cast shadows unless that is switched on

sablelightoverhaul.spotlight.lore.3: AFN channel reads numbers position by position: 0 on / 1 pitch / 2 yaw / 3 cone width / 4 intensity / 5 colour / 6 range / 7 falloff. A position the message does not reach keeps the lamps current value, so 1 30 90 just switches it on and aims it
sablelightoverhaul.spotlight.lore.4: AFN channel: a boolean alone switches the lamp and leaves the aim alone; text works too, written like the numbers with a colour list after a bar, of which this lamp takes the first. A channel made of two frequencies needs both boards -- fit one and look for (live) in the description
sablelightoverhaul.disco.lore.2: AFN channel reads numbers position by position: 0 on / 1 spin / 2 ray width / 3 intensity / 4 range / 5 beams / 6 falloff. Colours go after a bar, as on the balls own page, e.g. 1 20 8 15 64 12 0 | 3,7,11. A boolean alone only switches it
sablelightoverhaul.lightsource.lore.3: An AFN channel is a redstone strength to this lamp: only strength (0-15) is used, numbers and text are ignored. Channels hold their value, so there is no edge to catch

sablelightoverhaul.text.4eb07fe2aa555262:
Overall size multiplier for automatic muzzle flash particles, range 0.1~16: both flame length and half-width are multiplied by it, and it is the only master size switch. Particles are spawned as soon as muzzle flash data is received, regardless of lighting tier.
 Default: 4.7700000000000005
 Range: 0.1 ~ 16.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.b288d9979f62d60f:
Length multiplier of the flame along the muzzle axis, range 0.1~3: actual length = a random number from 0.65~0.9 × size multiplier × this value. It only changes the length of this one particle and does not affect light.
 Default: 0.7685
 Range: 0.1 ~ 3.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.7a5460facbe28c7c:
Multiplier for the flame's lateral half-width, range 0.1~3: actual half-width = a random number from 0.075~0.11 × size multiplier × this value. It only controls flame thickness and does not change length.
 Default: 1.2325
 Range: 0.1 ~ 3.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.dd36f3bde491e8fc:
Maximum opacity of flame particles, range 0.1~1.0: the cap is 1.0, so you cannot make it more solid; lower values make the flame more transparent. Read only once when the particle is spawned.
 Default: 0.7155000000000001
 Range: 0.1 ~ 1.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.7d7c4c5394eb41f8:
How many ticks an automatic muzzle flash particle survives, range 1~20: read only once at spawn; increasing it only makes the same flame linger longer, not brighter.
 Default: 3
 Range: 1 ~ 20
sablelightoverhaul.text.73b7bf24a6c852fa:
Number of angular lobes in the autocannon volumetric flame, 3~6, default 4. Only changes the contour of the same gas volume in VOLUME mode; does not add particles, draw calls, or smoke; works together with lobe strength.
 Default: 4
 Range: 3 ~ 6
sablelightoverhaul.text.669e31be676157a3:
Lobe strength of the autocannon volumetric flame, 0~1, default 0.65. 0 is the original continuous cone from 0.1.505, fully revertible; larger values make lobes more pronounced and the volume contour less smooth. Only effective in VOLUME mode; does not change brightness, light source, or smoke.
 Default: 1.0
 Range: 0.0 ~ 1.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.28c9fcd7d4a716ef:
Twist speed of the autocannon volumetric flame along the barrel axis and with age, 0~3, default 1.1. Higher values make lobe phase rotate more with age/length, reducing the static petal look; 0 keeps the phase fixed. Only effective in VOLUME mode.
 Default: 3.0
 Range: 0.0 ~ 3.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.814fc92e4bb89ba7:
Forward length variation between lobes of the autocannon volumetric flame, 0~1, default 0.55. Larger values make the tips of adjacent lobes more uneven, avoiding a neat star/flower cross-section; 0 makes all lobes the same length. Only effective in VOLUME mode.
 Default: 0.525
 Range: 0.0 ~ 1.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.17e748f6bbfe0543:
Lobe edge sharpness of the autocannon volumetric flame, 1~4, default 1.6. Larger values make lobes narrower with clearer gaps; too large reads as geometric petals, so try 1.3~2.0 first. Only effective in VOLUME mode.
 Default: 1.275
 Range: 1.0 ~ 4.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.55fe793d88842e2d:
Bright core convergence of the autocannon volumetric flame, 0~1, default 0.5. Larger values make the bright core narrower and more concentrated, so the outer lobes appear relatively more prominent; 0 keeps the original bright core width. Only effective in VOLUME mode.
 Default: 0.735
 Range: 0.0 ~ 1.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.c82d1cb0b6e99ba5:
Outer edge softening of the autocannon volumetric flame, 0~1, default 0.6. Larger values make the outer transition wider and more like cooling gas; smaller values make it harder. Only effective in VOLUME mode.
 Default: 0.495
 Range: 0.0 ~ 1.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.1303c90d09bd9c0e:
How long the automatic cannon muzzle light exists in the flash library, in ticks, range 1~40. Read by autoLight().
 Default: 5
 Range: 1 ~ 40
sablelightoverhaul.text.74abf784a59b5e41:
Distance from the light source along the muzzle axis until brightness reaches zero, in blocks, range 0.1~96: this is only the forward half-axis; brightness falls off earlier off-axis (big cannons use an ellipsoid, autocannons a rhombus — the normalized distances of the three axes are summed). Read by area lights in both Compatible and GPU tiers; not read in Legacy tier.
 Default: 32.0
 Range: 0.1 ~ 96.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.874dbeb4ac5e5c66:
Distance from the light source backward (toward the breech) until brightness reaches zero, in blocks, range 0.1~96; together with forwardRange it defines the total front-to-back length, and parts farther back than rearClipDistance are clipped.
 Default: 16.0
 Range: 0.1 ~ 96.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.aa1b03c68de60a0a:
Lateral radius of the light source, in blocks, range 0.1~96: both laterally and vertically it is widest at the light source and tapers along the muzzle axis. Big cannons scale proportionally with referenceSize; autocannons use a fixed size.
 Default: 16.0
 Range: 0.1 ~ 96.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.bccd5f5b8d49367b:
Vertical radius of the light source, in blocks, range 0.1~96, defaulting to the same as sideRange; referenced to the world vertical direction, it does not roll with the barrel, and only differs from sideRange if you want to flatten or stretch the light spot.
 Default: 16.0
 Range: 0.1 ~ 96.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.f25487cd31074b55:
How many blocks behind the light source the light is clipped entirely (approximating muzzle occlusion, not true occlusion), in blocks, range 0.0~96, scaled with size and capped by maximumRange: setting 0 kills all light behind the light source; setting >= rearRange is equivalent to disabling clipping.
 Default: 12.0
 Range: 0.0 ~ 96.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.924001602d5ae3b6:
Fraction of the normalized distance (0 = light source, 1 = light field boundary) kept at full brightness as the center, range 0~0.9: larger means a bigger hard core, 0 gives a purely soft-edged light spot; together with middleFraction and tailBrightness it forms the three-segment spatial falloff.
 Default: 0.25
 Range: 0.0 ~ 0.9
sablelightoverhaul.text.bdfc6c30b7698cb4:
Fraction of the remaining distance after the core occupied by the middle segment, range 0.05~0.95: smaller means brightness drops faster and more distance is left for the outer tail (the tail slope is always gentler than the middle segment).
 Default: 0.55
 Range: 0.05 ~ 0.95
sablelightoverhaul.text.d5b18b0feecfba1e:
Brightness at the end of the middle segment, range 0~0.9; it is actually clamped below (1-middleFraction)*0.95 so the outer tail falls off more gently than the middle segment — raising it above that limit will not make the outer ring white.
 Default: 0.2
 Range: 0.0 ~ 0.9
sablelightoverhaul.text.80bb4b6f1ea1e07e:
How many ticks this stage lasts, range 1~600; for big cannons blast and smoke are two consecutive stages, each timed from its own start (smoke begins only after the muzzle hold period ends). The Compatible tier also uses the sum of blast + smoke durations as the lifetime of the whole flash, so changing this directly changes how long the flash exists.
 Default: 5
 Range: 1 ~ 600
sablelightoverhaul.text.f42583f39ebf51e9:
Number of ticks brightness stays at full value after appearing, range 0~600, where 0 means decay starts immediately on appearance; it belongs to the same brightness curve as duration, decayPerTick, and minimumBrightness, and is read by both Compatible and GPU tiers.
 Default: 1
 Range: 0 ~ 600
sablelightoverhaul.text.da1328dccce70b82:
Lower limit of brightness decay, range 0~1: when greater than 0, a residual glow remains at the end of the stage until durationTicks elapses, then it goes out. It only applies within the brightness curve; when the Compatible tier composes the total lifetime for big cannons, that spot is treated as 0, so raising it does not extend how long the flash exists.
 Default: 0.0
 Range: 0.0 ~ 1.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.d8f2e6c778188cc3:
Fraction of initial brightness lost per tick after the hold period ends, range 0~1 (linear subtraction, not exponential decay): 0 means it stays bright until time runs out, 1 means it drops to minimumBrightness in a single tick.
 Default: 0.5
 Range: 0.0 ~ 1.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.009f3617849c47f1:
Autocannons do not use this setting: they have a fixed size, and the scale reference value is hardcoded to 1, so changing it has no effect.
 Default: 1.0
 Range: 0.1 ~ 64.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.35ff600e021d2017:
Upper limit for each radius after scaling, in blocks, range 1~96: forward/backward, lateral, and vertical radii plus rearClipDistance are all clamped by it, preventing an oversized light field when the propellant charge is too strong.
 Default: 32.0
 Range: 1.0 ~ 96.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.cc7227fe61ff2ba7: Continuous muzzle residual smoke: new smoke follows the muzzle while old smoke stays in the world. Independent of the blast smoke cloud, flash lighting, and tracer trails; disabling it clears the effect immediately. At most 8 emitters at once, each with 64 smoke puffs; increasing size and lifetime does not raise the count budget.
sablelightoverhaul.text.3a73de70bfa657b6:
Delay after firing before residual smoke starts, in seconds; applies only to new emitters.
 Default: 0.65
 Range: 0.0 ~ 10.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.9c54757bd6df1504:
Duration of continuous smoke emission, in seconds. Firing again refreshes the duration rather than stacking emitters indefinitely.

 Range: 0.1 ~ 30.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.e59af1f839d11e43:
How long each smoke puff persists after spawning, in seconds; the final disappearance time is roughly delay + emission time + persistence time.
 Default: 2.985

sablelightoverhaul.text.b88d9ee54bae9562:
Full diameter of the residual smoke outlet, in blocks, not radius.
 Default: 1.9975
 Range: 0.02 ~ 16.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.5eb2377fdbd1b44a:
Full diameter of the residual smoke after spreading, in blocks; independent of the original big smoke cloud size.
 Default: 5.9925
 Range: 0.02 ~ 16.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.e51e135431be1af3:
Speed along the muzzle direction at spawn, in blocks/sec; it then gradually slows and disperses.
 Default: 6.08
 Range: 0.0 ~ 32.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.9d502bc0ca72d049:
World upward drift speed of the smoke after cooling, in blocks/sec.
 Default: 1.02
 Range: 0.0 ~ 12.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.0c8c67dc0c5bfe7d:
Fraction of the muzzle's motion velocity inherited at spawn, including hull movement and turret traverse; it does not make old smoke keep following the muzzle.
 Default: 0.5
 Range: 0.0 ~ 1.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.88b3e81817ded712:
Strength of spatial swirling and lateral dispersion for the residual smoke; 0 disables lateral curl while keeping forward motion and rise.
 Default: 0.7
 Range: 0.0 ~ 8.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.f98630e5c825aec2:
Residual smoke density, 0~1; does not change existing muzzle smoke puffs.
 Default: 0.55
 Range: 0.0 ~ 1.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.b161e917a903a7b5:
Moves the residual smoke outlet forward along the current muzzle axis, in blocks. Default 0.15; can be increased when smoke passes through a barrel; follows muzzle rotation and CBCMW recoil, without changing shells, muzzle flash, or existing smoke puffs. Changes take effect immediately for newly emitted smoke points.
 Default: 0.15
 Range: 0.0 ~ 16.0
sablelightoverhaul.text.841fe4d3eed83423:
Lifetime override for visible tank fireballs, default 2 ticks, close to the brief deflagration of a big cannon; 0 uses the server's original lifetime. Only affects new fireballs; does not change smoke lifetime, brightness, or existing size multipliers.
 Default: 4
 Range: 0 ~ 40
sablelightoverhaul.text.6b892436fb01d58c: Tank main smoke and residual smoke use 64 pre-baked smoke shapes, with each puff lit on a single face; scene lighting is preserved, reducing repeated noise/shadow/per-light computation. Enabled by default; disabling restores the original three-slice soft smoke for comparison. Geometry, count, lifetime, and color settings are unchanged; the three lobes are composited in a shared local coordinate space.
sablelightoverhaul.text.42eecbf291406cee:
Tank smoke comparison mode. NATIVE: original vanilla cloud-smoke texture, fluffy growth, cooling, and at least 30 ticks of persistence, with spawn opacity set only by release progress; COMPACT: uses server lifetimes such as 18 ticks, the expansion cap, and extra per-particle fade-out. Both preserve the per-shot smoke budget, short travel, and depth-write-free sorting; only affects newly spawned smoke and does not modify existing config values.
Allowed Values: NATIVE, COMPACT
sablelightoverhaul.text.b37734fe2ebeef7e:
Overall geometry multiplier for tank cannon flames, 0.1~8, default 2; scales length and width together with the muzzle as the anchor, without changing brightness, smoke amount, or light radius; applies to both the baseline and the volumetric version.
 Default: 3.0020000000000002
 Range: 0.1 ~ 8.0

sablelightoverhaul.text.243dcb27ad379d73:

Those who want that volumetric feel can raise it themselves (0.25 / 0.5 / 1.0), and the trail comes back proportionally. **Affects fancy clouds only**: blocky clouds use d4's per-frame path, which has no temporal accumulation anyway.

With this on, distant particles blend into the pixel first and nearer ones cover them: smoke only tints what is behind it instead of erasing it. **Cost**: sorting each layer that considers itself translucent once per frame (opaque layers and NO_RENDER are skipped; cost grows as n log n with that layer's particle count, roughly a fraction of a millisecond to a millisecond at a full 16384 layer, and Iris calls render twice per frame, so it happens twice). **Side effect**: when the queue is full at 16384, vanilla would evict the oldest; after sorting it evicts the farthest.
